accessibility.pageSubtitle: How the Classroom 50 web app conforms to WCAG 2.2 Level AA, checked automatically on every build.

statement.heading: Accessibility statement
statement.intro: We want everyone to be able to use Classroom 50, including people who use a keyboard, a screen reader, or other assistive technology.
statement.target: We aim to meet WCAG 2.2 Level AA. Color contrast is checked on every build; the rest is checked by hand with a keyboard and a screen reader. The conformance report lists where we stand on each criterion.
statement.limitations: A few criteria are marked "Partially Supports" in the conformance report, each with a note on what's left to do. We fix these as work lands.

criteria.standardText: WCAG 2.2 — 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum, AA) for text, 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast for UI components. The palette follows GitHub's Primer primitives, which target Level AA.
criteria.marginWhy: We hold each pair a little above the WCAG minimum — headroom that absorbs anti-aliasing, sub-pixel rendering, and future palette tweaks. It's a recommendation, not required for conformance.
criteria.enhancedWhy: Each pair is also scored against the stricter 1.4.6 Enhanced floors (body ≥ {{body}}:1, large ≥ {{large}}:1). This is reported for transparency, not required — AA is the conformance target.

repoSource.label: Start with a template

none.label: No template
none.help: Create a fresh repository for each student.

template.label: Template repository
template.help: Generate each student's repository from a template you provide.

addReadme.label: Add a README
addReadme.helpOn: Start each repository with a README.md. This first commit is what lets branches, pull requests, and the Feedback PR work.
addReadme.helpOff: Start without a README. With the built-in autograder on, repositories still begin with the autograding files and grade normally. With it off, repositories are completely bare, and autograding and the Feedback PR are permanently unavailable.

includeAllBranches.label: Include all branches
includeAllBranches.help: Copy every branch and its history from the template, not just the default branch. This applies to students who accept from now on; repositories already created are not changed.

copyAbout.label: Copy About from template
copyAbout.help: Copy the template's About (its description) onto each student repository. GitHub does not copy it automatically. This applies to students who accept from now on; repositories already created are not changed.

copyTopics.label: Copy topics from template
copyTopics.help: Copy the template's topics onto each student repository. GitHub does not copy them automatically. This applies to students who accept from now on; repositories already created are not changed.

form.feedbackPrHelp: Open a pull request in each student's repository for inline review and comments on their work.
form.feedbackPrEmptyRepoHelp: Unavailable for empty repositories: there's no starter commit to compare a student's work against.

feedbackPrTemplate.label: Use the template's pull request template as the Feedback PR body
feedbackPrTemplate.help: Use the template repository's pull request template (.github/pull_request_template.md) as the body of each student's Feedback PR instead of the built-in one. You are responsible for the template's contents. If the file is missing or unreadable, the built-in body is used.
feedbackPrTemplate.checking: Checking the template for a pull request template…
feedbackPrTemplate.autoEnabled: Auto-enabled: a pull request template was found in the template repository.

studentPermission.label: Student repo access
studentPermission.help: The role each student is granted on their own assignment repository at accept time. Push (write) is the default. Choose Admin to let students manage repository settings and enable GitHub Pages. This applies to students who accept from now on; use the submissions page to change repositories already created.
studentPermission.groupHelp: Group members join with at least admin so the group owner can add teammates. This applies to repositories created from now on; use the submissions page to change existing ones.

autograding.editHelp: Changing the built-in autograder only affects repositories students accept from now on. Repositories already accepted keep their original setup, so you'll need to update the existing repositories yourself.

none.label: Do not use the built-in autograder
none.help: Grade with your own GitHub Actions workflow instead. With a template, add the workflow to it; without one, the assignment has no autograder.

built-in.label: Use the built-in autograder
built-in.help: Set up the built-in autograder, then add the tests and runtime below.

grading.label: Grading
grading.help: How this assignment is graded. "Autograded" runs the autograder you configure below. "Manual" lets you enter each student's score by hand on the submissions page. "Not graded" records no score.

maxPoints.label: Max points
maxPoints.help: Total points available for this manual assignment. Used to show each student's score out of the maximum.

submissionMode.label: Submission type
submissionMode.help: "Every push to the default branch" counts each student commit after the starter commit (the tool's own accept and autograding-update commits don't count). "A tagged commit" counts only tagged commits, so ordinary pushes use no Actions minutes; a student submits by pushing a tag or running gh student submit.
submissionMode.editWarning: Changing this only affects repositories created from now on. Repositories students already accepted keep the old setting until you update them. Use "Update autograding triggers" on the submissions page or gh teacher assignment submission-mode. Students must pull after the update.

choices.everyPush: Every push to the default branch

submissionTags.label: Submission tags
submissionTags.help: Optional tag names (one per line) whose commits also count, e.g. phase1, phase2. Patterns like v* match a family of tags. Leave empty for none.
submissionTags.wildcardCaution: A broad pattern like v* matches every tag a student pushes, including unrelated release tags. Prefer exact names like phase1.
submissionTags.commaHint: Put one tag per line, not a comma-separated list. A comma becomes part of the tag name and will be rejected.

repoFeatures.heading: Repository features
repoFeatures.help: Whether each student repository has Wikis, Issues, Projects, and Pull requests enabled.
repoFeatures.helpExisting: Changes apply to repositories created from now on. To update ones students already accepted, use the submissions page.
repoFeatures.templateContentWarning: Inheriting a private template also copies its Wiki, Issues, and Projects content, so keep answer keys out of a template you inherit from.
repoFeatures.overrideTemplate: The default follows the template's settings when a student accepts. Existing repositories won't change if you update the template later.
repoFeatures.overrideNoTemplate: The default keeps GitHub's own repository defaults.
repoFeatures.overrideExisting: To update repositories students already accepted, use the bulk repository-features action on the submissions page.

form.advancedHelp: Optional grading and runtime settings. Blank fields use their documented defaults.
form.dockerImageTip: Grade inside this public Docker image instead of a GitHub-hosted runner. The image provides the OS and its packages. It must be publicly pullable (for example ubuntu:24.04).
form.containerUserTip: The user the container runs as. Set root if checkout fails with a permission error. GitHub Actions runs container steps as the host runner's user, so a non-root image often can't write to the workspace.
form.setupCommandTip: Runs once before the other tests, for example to compile or install dependencies. A non-zero exit or timeout sets the autograde status to failure without changing the numeric score; later tests still run.
form.setupTimeoutTip: New setup commands start at {{default}} seconds. Set 0 to use the runner's 10-second default, or choose a whole number from 1 through {{max}}.
form.allowedFilesTip: Ordered {{gitignore}}-style patterns, one per line, defining which files belong to a submission (last match wins, {{bang}} re-includes). E.g. {{star}} then {{example}} allows only {{result}}. Blank allows every file.
form.releaseAssetsTip: One exact workspace-relative file path per line; paths are exact, not glob patterns, and may total at most 8 KiB of UTF-8 text. Files are collected after grading and attached on both passing and failing grades; missing files are skipped. Release filenames may use only ASCII letters, numbers, dots, underscores, and hyphens, and may not begin or end with a dot or contain consecutive periods.
form.passThresholdTip: Off by default. When on, the submissions page marks submissions passing or failing against the bar below (Passing rollup, score badges, passing/failing filter). This is a display threshold only. It does not change a student's actual score.

runner.label: GitHub runner
runner.tip: The GitHub Actions runner label(s) that grade this assignment. Blank uses ubuntu-latest. Combine comma-separated labels for a self-hosted runner (e.g., self-hosted, linux, x64).
runner.selfHostedHint: Combine comma-separated labels for a self-hosted runner (e.g., self-hosted, linux, x64).
runner.noRunnerMatch: No runner matches {{labels}}. Check the spelling.

runtime.envHostedHelp: Grades on a GitHub Actions runner.
runtime.envContainerHelp: Grades inside a public Docker image (it owns the OS packages).
runtime.languagesTip: Pick a version to install that toolchain (for example Node 26, Java 25), or type a custom one. A blank field skips it. Python defaults to 3.14 when blank on the hosted runner. You can enable as many toolchains as you need.
runtime.selfHostedDisabled: Ignored on a self-hosted runner, which uses its own prebuilt toolchains and packages. Provision these in the runner image instead.
runtime.versionTip: The {{language}} version to install (via the setup-{{language}} action). Leave blank to skip it. You can type any version the setup action accepts.
runtime.aptTip: Extra Ubuntu packages installed (apt-get) before grading, comma- or space-separated. Lowercase Debian package names.
runtime.runnerContainerError: "{{label}}" is a macOS/Windows runner; a Docker image needs an Ubuntu (or custom/self-hosted) runner.

template.okPrivate: Private template in {{owner}}, branch <branch>{{branch}}</branch>. Students can access it.

template.restrictedItemApprove: Approve Classroom 50 for {{owner}} (Org settings → Third-party access).

template.privateForkNoParent: {{owner}}/{{repo}} is a private fork (branch <branch>{{branch}}</branch>). <important>Important: the fork's upstream org must keep Classroom 50 approved — if that approval is ever removed, students will fail to accept (HTTP 403).</important> To avoid depending on the upstream org, use a fresh (non-fork) repo: create a new repo and copy the fork's contents into it.

rename.repoCount_one: {{count}} existing student repository will be renamed.
rename.repoCount_other: {{count}} existing student repositories will be renamed.

rename.failedSection: Failed ({{count}}) — fix the causes and finish the rename; it is safe to re-run

error.overBudget: “{{slug}}” still exceeds the repository-name budget for classroom “{{classroom}}”.
error.alreadyRenamed: This assignment was already renamed once (from “{{from}}”) — a rename is one-shot, so it can’t be renamed again.
error.fitsBudget: “{{slug}}” fits the repository-name budget — renaming is offered only to fix a slug whose student repository names can exceed GitHub’s limit.
error.slugTaken: “{{slug}}” already exists in {{classroom}} — choose a different slug.
error.slugReserved: “{{slug}}” is reserved: it is the pre-rename slug of “{{current}}” — choose a different slug.

error.treeTruncated: The classroom configuration repository is too large to list completely, so the autograder folder can’t be moved safely — rename with the CLI instead.

published.unlistedWarning: This classroom uses an unlisted URL: its resources are served at an unguessable path instead of a guessable one. This is obscurity, not access control — the link is the only thing guarding the data, anyone who has it can read the file, and links can leak (browser history, referrers, search crawlers). Share the per-assignment accept link or CLI command (which include the key) from each assignment's page.

banner.title: Everything below is served publicly over the internet
banner.body: Your classroom50 repository is private, but its GitHub Pages site is public by design — students and the autograder fetch these files without authenticating. Only the allow-listed files below are published; anything else in the repo (your roster, internal classroom fields, service token) stays private. A classroom can use an unlisted URL to make its files harder to find, but that is obscurity, not access control — the files are still public to anyone who has the link.

teardown.executeError: Teardown failed. Some repositories may not have been deleted.

teardown.forbidden: GitHub refused to delete repositories (403), and your permissions look sufficient. An organization policy or a protected repository is likely blocking the deletion. Check the organization's settings, then run teardown again.
teardown.forbiddenPartial_one: GitHub refused to delete repositories (403) after {{count}} was already deleted, and that deletion is permanent. overwrite.title: Update workflow files to keep grading working?
overwrite.body_one: 1 Classroom 50 workflow/script file in your classroom50 repository is out of date and will be refreshed:
overwrite.body_other: {{count}} Classroom 50 workflow/script files in your classroom50 repository are out of date and will be refreshed:

orgDefaults.title: Organization safety defaults
orgDefaults.what: Locks down organization member privileges to safe defaults (base permissions, repo creation, visibility changes, and related settings).
orgDefaults.why: Stops students from changing or deleting each other's repositories, or making private classroom work public.
orgDefaults.remediation: Open the org member-privileges page and apply the flagged settings by hand — some are controlled by an enterprise policy and can only be set there.

orgActions.title: Actions permissions
orgActions.what: Enables GitHub Actions for the organization.
orgActions.why: Autograding and the published assignment site run as Actions workflows, so they can't run until Actions is enabled.
orgActions.remediation: Open the org Actions settings and allow Actions to run (set the policy to allow all actions, or at minimum the workflows Classroom 50 ships).

orgBudget.title: Actions spending cap
orgBudget.what: Creates a $0 GitHub Actions spending cap (only if none exists).
orgBudget.why: A $0 hard-stop budget blocks paid Actions minutes, so a runaway autograde workflow can't run up a bill. An existing budget you set is left untouched.
orgBudget.remediation: Open the org billing budgets settings and set a $0 GitHub Actions budget with "prevent further usage" enabled (needs Organization Administration access).

orgPrCreation.title: Actions pull request creation
orgPrCreation.what: Allows GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests in the organization.
orgPrCreation.why: Some Classroom 50 workflows open pull requests on a student's behalf; without this they fail with a permissions error.
orgPrCreation.remediation: Open the org Actions settings and enable "Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests".

configRepo.title: classroom50 repository
configRepo.what: Creates the private classroom50 repository in the organization.
configRepo.why: Classroom 50 has no backend — this repo holds all classroom config, manifests, workflows, and scores.
configRepo.remediation: This is a required step. Re-run setup; if it keeps failing, confirm you have owner permissions and that an org/enterprise policy isn't blocking private repository creation.

skeleton.title: Workflow files
skeleton.what: Commits or updates the workflow and script files Classroom 50 needs in the classroom50 repository.
skeleton.why: These bundled files run autograding, publishing, and scoring; re-running setup also upgrades them to the latest version.
skeleton.remediation: This is a required step. Re-run setup; if it keeps failing, check that you can push to the classroom50 repository's default branch.

branchProtection.title: Branch protection
branchProtection.what: Protects the classroom50 repository's main branch.
branchProtection.why: Keeps the source-of-truth config and scores from being force-pushed or deleted.
branchProtection.remediation: Open the repository branch settings and protect the main branch, or re-run setup to re-apply it.

workflowPermissions.title: Workflow permissions
workflowPermissions.what: Sets the default GITHUB_TOKEN workflow permissions for the classroom50 repository.
workflowPermissions.why: Autograding and publishing workflows need write access to commit results and deploy Pages.
workflowPermissions.remediation: Open the repository Actions settings and set workflow permissions to read and write, or re-run setup.

reusableWorkflowAccess.title: Reusable workflow access
reusableWorkflowAccess.what: Allows other repositories in the org to use the reusable workflows in classroom50.
reusableWorkflowAccess.why: Assignment repos call the shared autograding workflow from classroom50; without access sharing, their runs fail.
reusableWorkflowAccess.remediation: Open the repository Actions settings and, under "Access", allow access from repositories in the organization. Or re-run setup.

pages.title: GitHub Pages
pages.what: Enables GitHub Pages for the classroom50 repository (built from Actions).
pages.why: Published assignment instructions and dashboards are served from this Pages site.
pages.remediation: Open the repository Pages settings and enable Pages with the GitHub Actions source. Pages from a private repo may require GitHub Team or Enterprise.

rulesets.title: Branch protection rulesets
rulesets.what: Creates organization rulesets that protect classroom and assignment repositories.
rulesets.why: Rulesets enforce the classroom guardrails (protected branches, restricted deletions) across every repo the org creates.
rulesets.remediation: Open the org rulesets page to review them, or re-run setup to re-apply. Rulesets may require GitHub Team or Enterprise.
